title: Invoice2go Review for Tradies: What Works (and the Typing + Cap Problem)
meta_title: Invoice2go Review for Tradies (2026) — Honest Take | SMASH
meta_description: Honest Invoice2go review for handymen and sole traders: solid mobile invoices, where monthly caps and tap-to-type slow real trade volume, and when a full quote→approve→pay loop fits better.
excerpt: Invoice2go is one of the apps our ICP actually uses. Here’s a fair review: what it does well, the pain points people search for, and when you need more than typed PDFs.
key_takeaways: Invoice2go is a legitimate mobile invoicer — templates, estimates, payments — used by real sole traders.
Two pain points dominate for trades: typing every line, and low monthly invoice caps on cheaper plans.
“Invoice sent” is not the same as quote → approve → invoice → paid on site.
Keep Invoice2go for tiny volume; change capture when you invoice multiple times a week.

faq_data.question: Is Invoice2go good for tradies?
faq_data.answer: It makes professional invoices from a phone. For trade volumes, the cheap plans’ invoice caps are tight, and every document is still typed. Fine for very low volume; painful for several jobs a week.

faq_data.question: How many invoices can you send on Invoice2go?
faq_data.answer: Plans change — historically Starter was only a couple of invoices per month on monthly billing, with higher tiers unlocking more. Always check Invoice2go’s current pricing page before you decide.

faq_data.question: What is the biggest Invoice2go pain on site?
faq_data.answer: Capture speed. Forms on a phone between jobs. That is when estimates wait until tonight and jobs get forgotten.

faq_data.question: What is a fair Invoice2go alternative?
faq_data.answer: If the pain is typing or caps, look for unlimited-enough workflow with voice or catalog pricing and customer approval on the send. See our SMASH vs Invoice2go page.

faq_data.question: Should I leave Invoice2go overnight?
faq_data.answer: No. Trial the next quote on a faster tool, keep Invoice2go until you trust the loop.

content:
## Short answer

**Invoice2go is a real mobile invoicer our ICP uses. Typing + plan caps are the trade-offs.**

This is an honest founder review — not a teardown. Invoice2go has helped a lot of freelancers and contractors send branded invoices from a phone. If you are a handyman, cleaner, or mobile trade doing several jobs a week, the questions that matter are: how long does each document take, and does the cheap plan even let you send enough?

Deep comparison (pricing checked carefully): [SMASH vs Invoice2go](/vs-invoice2go) · [Voice to invoice](/voice-invoicing) · [For handymen](/for-handymen).

## Watch the 60-second demo

See the full loop — talk → verify your rates → send → they approve and pay:

[Watch the SMASH demo on YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=uNL733tYTf0) · [How voice to invoice works](/voice-invoicing)

## What Invoice2go does well

- **Mobile invoices people recognise** — logo, templates, estimates, payments
- **Estimate → invoice path** — you are not inventing a workflow from scratch
- **Familiar “simple app” category** — low learning curve for sole traders coming off Excel
- **Cheap entry** — the lowest paid tier can make sense if you truly send almost nothing

Plenty of people are happy on Invoice2go. That is allowed.

## What people are actually searching for (the pain points)

| Pain they feel | What they type (roughly) | Real job-to-be-done |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Hit the monthly cap | invoice2go invoice limit / only 2 invoices | Volume that matches trade life |
| Typing on site | invoice2go slow / type invoice on phone | Capture without forms |
| Worth the money? | is invoice2go worth it / invoice2go review | Fair pros/cons |
| Looking to switch | invoice2go alternative | Process fit |
| Full loop | estimate approve pay | Quote → approve → invoice → paid |

We already have a long-form vs page that digs into caps and pricing: [SMASH vs Invoice2go](/vs-invoice2go). This review is the pain-search twin — same ICP as Invoice Simple and Joist users.

## Where it breaks for people who work with their hands

### 1. Caps vs trade volume

A handyman can burn a “two invoices a month” style plan before Tuesday lunch. Paying up for unlimited while still typing every line is the classic fork. Numbers move — verify on Invoice2go — but the *shape* of the problem stays: cheap plans under-serve busy solos.

### 2. Typing is still the product

Invoice2go is forms. Good forms. Forms on a phone after a gutter clean still take minutes you do not have. SMASH’s bet is talk for ~30 seconds against [your rates](/materials-pricing), verify, send. Same category (mobile quoting/invoicing), different input.

### 3. PDF sent ≠ process finished

Estimates can be approved in many apps. The loop trades need is: priced quote while they wait → approve → invoice same lines → pay → you know they opened it. Scorecard lives on the [vs page](/vs-invoice2go).

## A real week on the tools

Same driveway reality as [Invoice Simple](/blog/invoice-simple-review-for-tradies): multiple small jobs, dirty hands, customer still there. Caps make it worse — you are not only typing; you are counting documents. That is how people start googling “invoice2go alternative” even when they like the app.

## Caps, pricing honesty, and what to verify yourself

Plan names and invoice counts change. Do not treat any competitor review (including this one) as a live price sheet. Open Invoice2go’s pricing page the day you decide, count how many invoices you actually send in a normal fortnight, and ask: *am I buying unlimited-enough volume, or am I still paying to type?*

If you are already on a higher tier and still batching Sunday admin, the problem is not the cap — it is capture. That is the same fork we describe for [Invoice Simple](/blog/invoice-simple-review-for-tradies): enough documents is necessary; speed is what stops the backlog.

## At a glance — what works / what doesn’t

| Need | Invoice2go | Gap for busy solos |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Clean mobile invoice | Strong | — |
| Low-volume cheap entry | Strong | Caps bite fast |
| Dirty-hands capture | Forms | Voice |
| Unlimited-enough volume | Higher tiers | Flat paid plans |
| Catalog materials (AU) | Manual | Built-in + your rates |
| Approve + pay loop | Partial | One portal link |
| Desk quote from Gmail | App-first | [Chrome extension](/chrome-extension) |

## Who should keep Invoice2go

- You send one or two invoices a month for real
- You like their templates / mini-site extras
- Typing does not bother you
- You are deep in their ecosystem and switching cost is high

## Who should look past it

- You quote multiple times a week ([handymen](/for-handymen), cleaners, gardeners)
- You keep hitting plan limits
- Quotes die because you are still typing in the ute — [first quote wins](/blog/first-quote-wins-instant-quote-on-site)

## Fair alternative (without trash-talk)

If the pain is **capture + volume + loop**, try voice against your catalog, then let the customer approve and pay. That is [SMASH vs Invoice2go](/vs-invoice2go). Start free; keep Invoice2go until you are sure.

Older vs post (still live): [SMASH vs Invoice2go blog](/blog/smash-vs-invoice2go).

## Bottom line

Invoice2go is good at typed mobile invoices. Our ICP often needs **enough volume** and a **faster process** — not a prettier form. Be honest which problem you have.
